subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Problems on trains II — mixed tiers
description: Train passing pole, platform, person, opposite-direction, same-direction crossing

questions.stem: A train 150 m long is moving at 54 km/h. The time it takes to pass a stationary pole is:
questions.explanation: Speed = 54 km/h = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. Time = length / speed = 150 / 15 = 10 s. Distractor 8 s comes from 150/18.75 (used 67.5 km/h). Distractor 12 s from 150/12.5. Distractor 15 s confuses the speed with the time directly.

questions.stem: A train 200 m long is travelling at 72 km/h. How long does it take to cross a platform 100 m long?
questions.explanation: When crossing a platform, the train covers (its own length + platform length) = 200 + 100 = 300 m. Speed = 72 km/h = 20 m/s. Time = 300 / 20 = 15 s. Distractor 12 s only counts platform length (100/8.33). Distractor 18 s from 360/20 (added an extra 60 m by mistake). Distractor 20 s = (200+200)/20 (over-counts platform).

questions.stem: Two trains, each 120 m long, are running in OPPOSITE directions at 36 km/h and 54 km/h. The time taken to cross each other completely is:
questions.explanation: Opposite direction → relative speed = sum = 36 + 54 = 90 km/h = 90 × 5/18 = 25 m/s. Combined length = 120 + 120 = 240 m. Time = 240 / 25 = 9.6 s. Distractor 12 s from 240/20 (used 72 km/h relative). Distractor 16 s from 240/15 (used 54 km/h alone). Distractor 24 s from 240/10 (used 36 km/h alone).

questions.stem: Two trains 150 m and 100 m long are moving in the SAME direction at 60 km/h and 40 km/h. The faster train overtakes the slower in:
questions.explanation: Same direction → relative speed = difference = 60 − 40 = 20 km/h = 20 × 5/18 = 50/9 m/s ≈ 5.56 m/s. Combined length = 150 + 100 = 250 m. Time = 250 / (50/9) = 250 × 9/50 = 45 s. Distractor 30 s would require 60 km/h relative speed (treats it as opposite direction). Distractor 60 s from 250/4.17 (used wrong conversion). Distractor 90 s = double the correct value.

questions.stem: A train passes a person walking at 5 km/h in the SAME direction in 9 seconds. If the train is 150 m long, the speed of the train is:
questions.explanation: Relative speed of train w.r.t. person = 150 m / 9 s = 50/3 m/s = 50/3 × 18/5 = 60 km/h. Since train and person are in same direction, relative speed = train speed − 5 km/h. So train speed = 60 + 5 = 65 km/h. Distractor 55 km/h subtracts 5 instead of adding (wrong direction). Distractor 75 km/h adds 15 (wrong magnitude). Distractor 60 km/h forgets to add the person's speed.

questions.stem: A 180-m-long train crosses a bridge in 24 seconds at 45 km/h. The length of the bridge is:
questions.explanation: Speed = 45 × 5/18 = 12.5 m/s. Total distance covered in 24 s = 12.5 × 24 = 300 m. This equals (train + bridge) = 180 + bridge. So bridge = 300 − 180 = 120 m. Distractor 100 m from 280 − 180 (used 11.67 m/s wrongly). Distractor 150 m = total/2 (forgot subtract). Distractor 180 m equals the train length (assumes bridge equals train).

questions.stem: A train running at 90 km/h crosses a man running at 9 km/h in the OPPOSITE direction in 4 seconds. The length of the train is:
questions.explanation: Opposite direction → relative speed = 90 + 9 = 99 km/h = 99 × 5/18 = 27.5 m/s. Length = relative speed × time = 27.5 × 4 = 110 m. Distractor 90 m comes from using 90 km/h alone. Distractor 100 m = 90 km/h × 4 s ÷ 18/5 (rounded). Distractor 125 m = 31.25 × 4 (used 112.5 km/h).
